items.title: Build a budget that works for you
items.description: Give every rupee a purpose without losing sight of everyday life.
items.objectives: Separate needs from wants;Build a monthly plan;Review irregular expenses
items.content:
A budget is a plan for your income. Begin with money you can reliably expect, then list essentials such as food, rent and transport. Separate flexible spending from commitments. If income varies, use a conservative estimate rather than your best month.

Set aside money for future expenses before deciding what is available to spend. A budget should include irregular costs, such as annual fees, repairs and festivals. Review actual spending every week and adjust the plan when circumstances change. A shortfall is a signal to revisit the plan, not a personal failure.
items.example: Illustrative example: with ₹20,000 monthly income, planned expenses of ₹15,000 leave ₹5,000 for goals and unexpected costs. These numbers are an example, not a recommended allocation.
items.takeaways: Track before you cut;Plan for irregular costs;Review your budget regularly

items.title: Banking, without the jargon
items.description: Understand accounts, interest and the documents behind them.
items.objectives: Compare account features;Understand interest;Protect account access
items.content:
A bank account helps you receive, hold and transfer money. Before opening one, compare service charges, minimum balance rules, access options and the terms of the account. A savings account and a current account serve different needs.

Interest is the amount paid for using money over time. Read the rate and how it is calculated. Banks may ask for identity and address documents under their verification processes. Use the bank’s official website or branch to confirm current requirements. Never share a PIN, password or one-time password with someone claiming to help.
items.example: Compare two hypothetical accounts: one has a service fee and the other has withdrawal limits. Which fits your actual usage?
items.takeaways: Read charges and conditions;Use official channels;Keep authentication details private

items.title: Your first emergency fund
items.description: Create a buffer for costs you cannot predict.
items.objectives: Define an emergency;Choose accessible savings;Set a manageable goal
items.content:
An emergency fund is money reserved for unexpected essential expenses or a temporary loss of income. It is different from money saved for a planned purchase. Start with an amount you can maintain and build gradually.

Access and stability matter when choosing where to keep an emergency fund. A product with a lock-in period or fluctuating value may be unsuitable for immediate needs. The right target depends on your essential expenses, income stability and family responsibilities. Review it when those circumstances change.
items.example: If essential expenses are ₹12,000 a month, one month of expenses is ₹12,000. This is a planning example, not a universal target.
items.takeaways: Start small;Keep emergency money accessible;Replenish after using it

items.title: Fixed and recurring deposits
items.description: Compare lump-sum saving with regular contributions.
items.objectives: Distinguish FD and RD;Read withdrawal terms;Compare maturity values
items.content:
A fixed deposit generally places a lump sum for an agreed term. A recurring deposit generally involves periodic contributions. Both require you to understand the institution’s terms, interest calculation and maturity conditions.

Before committing, check early withdrawal rules, charges and taxation with the provider. Compare products using the same time period and contribution assumptions. A quoted annual rate alone does not tell you everything about access or final proceeds.
items.example: A lump sum available today and a monthly surplus are different cash flows. Match the product to the cash flow before comparing rates.
items.takeaways: Match saving patterns;Check access restrictions;Read current terms

items.title: Understand the Public Provident Fund
items.description: Learn the purpose of PPF and what to verify before opening an account.
items.objectives: Recognize a long-term product;Find official terms;Check access rules
items.content:
Public Provident Fund is a government small-savings product listed by India Post. It is intended for long-term saving. It should not be confused with an ordinary transaction account or an emergency cash balance.

Before choosing PPF, read the current official rules on eligibility, deposits, maturity, withdrawal and taxation. Rates and rules can change. This lesson does not quote a current rate or promise an individual tax benefit. Use the official source in the scheme explorer for the latest details.
items.example: A learner saving for a distant goal should compare access restrictions with a learner who may need the money next month.
items.takeaways: Verify official terms;Consider your time horizon;Do not assume instant access

items.title: Retirement planning and NPS
items.description: Understand contributions, investment risk and retirement income.
items.objectives: Explain contribution-based pensions;Identify investment risk;Find current NPS rules
items.content:
Retirement planning considers expenses after regular employment income changes or stops. A contribution-based system builds a retirement balance from contributions and investment outcomes. The National Pension System is regulated by PFRDA.

Investment-linked returns can vary. Contributions, charges, investment choices and withdrawal conditions all matter. Read official NPS information before deciding. This lesson does not predict returns or state that NPS suits every learner.
items.example: Compare a predictable expense in retirement with an uncertain future investment value. A plan needs room for uncertainty.
items.takeaways: Begin with your needs;Understand investment risk;Verify exit and withdrawal terms

items.title: Saving for a child’s future
items.description: Explore Sukanya Samriddhi through official information.
items.objectives: Identify long-term goals;Find eligibility rules;Compare access needs
items.content:
India Post lists the Sukanya Samriddhi Account among government small-savings products. Understanding a product begins with its purpose and official eligibility rules. Do not assume a scheme applies solely because its name sounds relevant.

Verify the current age conditions, account-opening requirements, deposit limits, maturity and withdrawal rules with an official provider. Keep education savings and immediate household needs in separate plans where practical.
items.example: A family can write down a future education goal, when money is needed, and the rules that must be checked before choosing a product.
items.takeaways: Check eligibility;Match the goal date;Keep official records

items.title: Insurance: protection before promises
items.description: Make sense of premiums, coverage and exclusions.
items.objectives: Explain risk pooling;Read exclusions;Distinguish insurance and investment
items.content:
Insurance transfers specified risks under a contract in exchange for a premium. The policy wording defines covered events, exclusions, limits and the claims process. A low premium alone does not establish whether coverage meets your needs.

Read waiting periods, deductibles and co-payment clauses where applicable. Disclose requested information accurately and keep policy records accessible. Ask the insurer to clarify uncertain clauses in writing. Insurance decisions depend on the actual policy and personal circumstances.
items.example: A policy may cover a loss but require the customer to pay a deductible. Read both the coverage and the customer’s share.
items.takeaways: Read the policy wording;Understand exclusions;Keep claims records

items.title: Income tax basics
items.description: Learn the vocabulary before you approach a tax return.
items.objectives: Distinguish income and tax;Understand records;Find official guidance
items.content:
Taxable income is determined by applicable rules, not simply by the balance in a bank account. Income sources, exemptions, deductions and the chosen regime can affect a calculation. Current rules must be checked for the relevant financial year.

Keep records of income, deductions claimed and tax already paid. This educational lesson does not calculate your tax or recommend a regime. Use the official Income Tax portal and qualified help when your circumstances require it.
items.example: A salary credit and a transfer between your own accounts have different meanings. Accurate records help distinguish them.
items.takeaways: Use the correct financial year;Keep supporting records;Verify current rules

items.title: Prepare for tax filing
items.description: Organize your information before submitting a return.
items.content:
Tax filing starts with understanding your income sources and selecting the applicable return under current rules. Gather statements and supporting records before entering figures. Prefilled information still needs to be checked.

Use the official portal to review filing and verification requirements. Retain the acknowledgement and evidence supporting the figures submitted. This lesson is a general workflow and does not assert an individual deadline or filing obligation.
items.example: Create a checklist of income statements, tax-paid records and supporting evidence, then reconcile differences before submission.
items.takeaways: Check prefilled information;Complete required verification;Retain supporting evidence

items.title: Digital payments with confidence
items.description: Check the recipient, amount and purpose before paying.
items.objectives: Recognize authorization;Review recipient details;Keep transaction references
items.content:
Digital payments can move money quickly. Before authorizing a transfer, check the recipient and amount on your own device. A request to enter a payment PIN is an authorization step and should not be treated as a way to receive a reward.

Use official applications and keep your device updated. If a transaction is unexpected, contact the provider through an independently verified support channel. Save the transaction reference and avoid sending further money to recover a disputed payment.
items.example: Pause when a stranger asks you to scan a code and enter a PIN to receive money. Verify the request through your provider.
items.takeaways: Read before approving;Use trusted apps;Keep transaction references

items.title: Spot a financial scam
items.description: Recognize urgency, impersonation and unrealistic promises.
items.content:
Scams often create urgency or promise exceptional rewards. A familiar logo or caller name is not proof of identity. Stop and verify through a channel you obtained independently, such as the official provider’s website or branch.

Do not install remote-access software at a stranger’s request or share authentication codes. If you suspect fraud, preserve messages and transaction details and promptly contact your bank through official channels. Reporting does not guarantee recovery, but records can help investigation.
items.example: A message threatens to close an account today unless you open a link. Visit the bank’s official site independently instead.
items.takeaways: Pause under pressure;Verify independently;Never disclose authentication codes

items.title: Navigate government schemes
items.description: Find reliable information and check whether a scheme is relevant.
items.objectives: Locate official sources;Separate discovery and eligibility;Prepare questions
items.content:
A scheme explorer can help discover programmes, but a search result is not an eligibility decision. Eligibility depends on current official rules and the applicant’s circumstances. Be wary of agents promising guaranteed approval.

Use official information to confirm the beneficiary group, application procedure and required documents. Requirements can differ by scheme and region. Keep an application acknowledgement and follow up through the official channel.
items.example: Write down the scheme name, source URL, date checked and questions to confirm before applying.
items.takeaways: Discovery is a starting point;Check official eligibility;Keep application records

sources.title: Understand the Public Provident Fund
sources.excerpt:
Public Provident Fund is a government small-savings product listed by India Post. It is intended for long-term saving. It should not be confused with an ordinary transaction account or an emergency cash balance.

Before choosing PPF, read the current official rules on eligibility, deposits, maturity, withdrawal and taxation. Rates and rules can change. This lesson does not quote a current rate or promise an individual tax benefit. Use the official source in the scheme explorer for the latest details.
